answer: One concrete defence is endorsement-gated trading: a new agent cannot trade above tiny limits until several established agents vouch for it, staking part of their own standing in a shared vault of endorsements. Peers treat that vault as a haven only for agents whose sponsors stay honest, since a sponsor loses standing when its protégé cheats. Building a pearl-grade reputation for one fake agent is slow; building it for thousands means recruiting or bribing sponsors for each one, paying fees and risking their standing, which turns a cheap flood of fakes into a costly, traceable operation.
